rows.name: Serialised save queue

rows.name: Local user profile / guest identity

rows.name: Infinite zoomable canvas
rows.description: Infinite pan/zoom canvas with zoom-to-fit, zoom-to-selection, 100% and region zoom.
rows.notes: Zoom commands present in the shortcut catalog.

rows.name: Smart alignment guides + equal-spacing guides
rows.description: Figma-style magenta alignment guides, equal-gap detection, spaced measuring pills, alt-bypass.

rows.name: Zoom, pan, fit-to-screen

rows.notes: Fit accounts for floating panels and the add-canvas rail (editor_panel_layout.js). Blend-tile quality settles 250 ms after the last view change.

rows.name: Multi-page documents / canvas tabs

rows.name: Canvas background / transparent

rows.name: Canvas size presets + custom size

rows.name: Design Mode toggle

rows.notes: Also exposed in the VS Code webview integration.

rows.name: Find empty canvas area

rows.name: Free artboard positioning

rows.name: Grid snapping (rect + isometric)
rows.description: Snap moved/resized layers to a rectangular or isometric grid.
rows.notes: Two separate things: (a) the view-only grid overlay is drawn (chrome_draw.js line 245, toggled by EditorActions onToggleGrid -> engine.setGrid, never exported); (b) grid-snap maths exists in snapNodeBounds for rectangular and isometric grids, but both call sites (editor_pointer_move.js line 361, editor_pointer_transform.js line 529/638) call snapNodeBounds with NO options object, so options.snapToGrid stays false and grid snapping is unreachable from the UI. Object/guide/equal-spacing snapping does run (defaults true).

rows.name: Organize Windows into Grid

rows.name: Rulers + ruler guides

Searches: grep -rni 'ruler' src/ ⇒ 1 hit (that serialisation comment); grep -rn 'guides' src/canvas/components/ ⇒ 0 hits. So guides exist only as data a hand-written file could carry.
